title: PyTorch
subtitle: ActiveKV extends PyTorch's XPU backend and ATen from native code; the capabilities model is a PyTorch fine-tune.

lede: I work with PyTorch from both ends: as a native extension that must be indistinguishable from the code it replaced, and as a training tool where the recipe, the size and the rebuild cost are measured choices. I work below the framework when the framework is in the way. In ActiveKV a native engine manages a model's key-value cache inside vLLM, which is built on PyTorch, so the engine has to speak PyTorch's tensor model exactly. I built it in C++ against ATen, PyTorch's tensor library, and registered its operators with PyTorch's own operator registry, so vLLM's attention path calls them as first-class operators.
quote: Profiles built on framework events are checked against an uninstrumented run before I believe them.
evidence: PyTorch native extension development: C++ operators on ATen registered in PyTorch's own registry across 22 source files, indistinguishable from the Python version bit for bit.
LLM fine-tuning: a full fine-tune of every parameter of a ~596 M-parameter model in 2 to 14 minutes, peaking at 17.6 GiB on one NVIDIA Blackwell GPU.
GPU profiling methodology: a conclusion built on timing-enabled events retracted once the events were shown to serialise the copy engine they observed.
